P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Individuals are free to carry out any kind of foreign-exchange transaction; reporting applies above USD 10,000 (Deloitte 2026). Banks offer dollar current accounts: Santander's is exclusive to clients with a peso current account (no minimum seniority), and Banco de Chile offers one too (Rankia). Approval usually depends on the bank's commercial evaluation and source-of-funds questions (search summary).

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Independent professionals file the 'inicio de actividades' with the SII (Servicio de Impuestos Internos) online via sii.cl, using an SII password (Clave Tributaria) or ClaveÚnica. It must be done within 2 months of starting the activity, or the SII can fine you. You then issue electronic boletas de honorarios through Mi SII (mandatory electronic since 2018). In 2026 the withholding/retention on boletas is 15.25% (Ley 21.133 phase-in).

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: Official TIN description supplied by Chile to the OECD: "All individuals and en tities that, due to their activities or condition , are or may be taxed in Chile, must be registered in the Rol Unico Tributario (RUT or TIN Registry- Article 66 of the Tax Code). This requirement applies to the carry -on of business activities in Chile, performance of dependent or independent personal services within the country, and investments in debt and equity instruments, amongst others." How a freelancer applies (forms, online portal, fees) was not captured.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: No special freelancer tax discount was found. The key regime for freelancers is the boleta de honorarios: the withholding on fees is 15.25% in 2026 (14.5% in 2025), rising to 16% in 2027 and 17% in 2028 under Law 21.133. sii.cl applies it automatically when you issue an electronic boleta (SII). The withholding is an advance payment settled in the annual income-tax return (general rule, not captured here).

D1_id_document.question: Identity documents residents use for KYC (gateways, banks, platforms)
D1_id_document.answer: National identity card: Cédula de identidad (Identity card) (Wikipedia, compulsory-ID list). Normally this is first issued at age 2 or 3, but it can be issued whenever the legal ascendant(s) request its issue. Banks and payment platforms usually also accept a passport; their exact lists were not captured. Foreign residents get a cédula de identidad para extranjeros from the Registro Civil, showing their RUN (national ID number) and visa (ChileAtiende).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (6) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
